intro: This week’s intelligence digest highlights key moves in retail and AI, including Walmart-backed Flipkart and Amazon intensifying their quick-commerce and AI infrastructure investments in India. Additionally, major tech players like Google and Amazon are advancing custom AI chip development and app store reforms, signaling a shift toward greater innovation and market expansion.

readOneThing.title: Walmart-backed Flipkart expands quick-commerce push as Amazon ramps up in India

items.title: Walmart-backed Flipkart expands quick-commerce push as Amazon ramps up in India
bullets: Flipkart's Minutes service has established 1,000 micro-fulfillment centers across India less than two years after its launch, aiming to expand to 1,500 by 2026.
Orders on Flipkart Minutes have increased approximately 400% year-over-year, with customer retention rising 20%, driven by demand beyond groceries into electronics and beauty products.
India's quick-commerce market features over 5,500 dark stores, with expectations to reach 7,500 by 2030 as companies like Amazon and Flipkart expand rapidly into smaller cities.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: Walmart-backed Flipkart has expanded its quick-commerce operations in India by surpassing 1,000 micro-fulfillment centers, while Amazon is simultaneously intensifying its quick-commerce efforts in the country.

items.title: Behold, the most realistic golf game ever  | Dominik Diamond
bullets: Normal Golf Game, created by Luke Muscat, is a golf video game designed to be the most challenging and realistic simulation of the sport to date.
The demo of Normal Golf Game includes only one hole and took the reviewer 428 strokes and nearly two hours to complete due to its difficult controls.
This game represents a new trend in gaming where control methods are intentionally made complex to closely replicate real-life sports experiences.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: In "Behold, the most realistic golf game ever," Dominik Diamond reviews Normal Golf Game, praising it for transforming an easy genre into a challenging experience that captures the complexities of playing golf. Despite the game's difficulty, the author appreciates the authentic representation of the sport's leisurely and social aspects.

items.title: Beyond Nvidia: Why AI giants like OpenAI, Google and Amazon are building custom chips
bullets: OpenAI has introduced Jalapeño, its first in-house AI inference chip developed with Broadcom and manufactured by TSMC, for internal deployment.
Custom inference chips help reduce operational costs by optimizing hardware for high-volume AI workloads, addressing the expensive deployment phase of generative AI.
Tech giants like Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta have long developed proprietary AI chips, making custom silicon a standard practice alongside Nvidia's dominant GPUs.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: Tech giants including OpenAI, Google, Amazon, and Microsoft are developing custom chips to reduce deployment costs and gain control over AI infrastructure, signaling a strategic shift beyond relying solely on Nvidia's GPUs for training in the competitive AI landscape.

items.title: C.P. Company Men’s Spring 2027: Behind the Seams
bullets: C.P. Company showcased its Spring 2027 men's ready-to-wear collection at Paris Men's Fashion Week, blending archival designs with new innovations.
The collection featured replicas of the 1988 Mille Miglia goggle jacket with a sun-faded look and introduced a newly developed 3D camo fabric made by acid-melting nylon.
Since 2021, the brand has engaged its community through the Behind the Seams project, inviting members to visit its Italian facilities and interact with archival garments.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: C.P. Company's Men's Spring 2027 collection, featured in WWD on June 27, 2026, draws inspiration from the brand’s archival Mille Miglia outerwear, showcasing a blend of luxury and heritage design elements.

items.title: Google Cuts App Store Fees, Opens Up External Payments
bullets: Google will reduce its Google Play fees and allow developers to use external payment systems and link to their own websites starting June 30.
The new fee structure introduces a 10% commission on the first $1 million in annual earnings from new installs, with higher rates applying thereafter.
These changes will initially take effect in the U.S., UK, and Europe, with plans for a broader global rollout over time following legal and regulatory pressures.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: Google announced a reduction in its Google Play app store fees and will permit developers to use external payment systems and link to their own websites, marking a significant change for app developers. This move addresses longstanding developer concerns over proprietary billing on major app platforms.

items.title: Amazon ups India bet with fresh $13B AI infrastructure investment
bullets: Amazon announced a $13 billion investment to expand its AI and cloud infrastructure in India through 2030, focusing on data centers in Mumbai and Hyderabad.
This investment is part of Amazon's total $48 billion commitment to India, including previous pledges made in 2023 and 2025.
Other global tech companies like Microsoft and Google have also pledged billions to develop AI and data center infrastructure in India by the end of the decade.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: On June 25, 2026, TechCrunch reported that Amazon is increasing its investment in India’s AI infrastructure with a fresh $13 billion commitment, reflecting the broader trend of global tech companies expanding their AI presence in the country.

items.title: Lowe’s makes it easier to order decorative geese, above-ground pools and other marketplace items in over 1,700 stores
bullets: Lowe’s integrated its third-party marketplace into the My Red Vest software, enabling store associates to help customers order marketplace items in over 1,700 stores.
Since launching its marketplace in late 2024, Lowe’s has more than doubled its assortment and added thousands of new items weekly, contributing to a 15.5% rise in online sales in Q1 2026.
The marketplace integration, reaching roughly 97% of Lowe’s stores, supports both consumer and professional customers and helps identify products for potential in-store stocking.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: Lowe's has integrated its third-party marketplace into My Red Vest, the in-store employee software, making it easier to order items like decorative geese and above-ground pools in over 1,700 stores.
